info.brief:
Encode Lua values and decode custom binary data in the
[MessagePack format](https://msgpack.org/index.html).

Decoding parses directly into Lua tables and strings without an intermediate
native tree. Container nesting is limited to 64 levels.
info.description:
Encode Lua values and decode custom binary data in the

Decoding parses directly into Lua tables and strings without an intermediate

elements.name: messagepack.decode
elements.description:
Decode exactly one complete MessagePack value. Malformed, truncated,
trailing or unsupported data raises a Lua error.

Nil becomes Lua nil by default. Use `decode_null_as_userdata` to retain
null fields and array entries as `messagepack.null`. Arrays become
tables indexed from 1; maps become tables. Duplicate keys use the last
value. Keys must be representable in Lua; nil and NaN keys are rejected.
The null option also permits a MessagePack nil key as the sentinel.

All integer and floating formats become Lua numbers. Lua's double
precision representation can round integers beyond its exact integer
range. String and binary formats both become binary-safe Lua strings.
Empty arrays and maps both become empty tables. Extension types,
including timestamps, are unsupported.

parameters.name: bytes
parameters.doc: MessagePack bytes; embedded NUL bytes are supported.

fields.name: decode_null_as_userdata
fields.doc: Preserve nil values as messagepack.null. Defaults to false.

elements.examples:
local bytes = assert(sys.load_resource("/data/config.msgpack"))
local config = messagepack.decode(bytes)
local bytes = messagepack.encode({1, messagepack.null, 3})
local values = messagepack.decode(bytes, {
    decode_null_as_userdata = true
})
assert(values[2] == messagepack.null)

elements.name: messagepack.encode
elements.description:
Encode one Lua value into a binary MessagePack string.

Dense tables with exactly the integer keys `1..n` become arrays.
Sparse, mixed-key and other tables become maps. Empty tables default
to maps; `encode_empty_table_as_map = false` changes all empty tables
in this call to arrays. Raw entries are used without table metamethods.
Map order is unspecified. Shared tables are serialized independently;
cyclic tables and nesting beyond 64 containers raise errors.

Exactly integral numbers within the signed/unsigned 64-bit ranges use
the smallest integer format. Other numbers use float64. Negative zero,
NaN and infinities are preserved. Lua strings use the MessagePack string
format and retain every byte; decoding and re-encoding a binary-format
value therefore changes its tag to a string tag.

Only `messagepack.null` (also `json.null`) is supported as userdata.
Functions, threads and other userdata raise errors.

parameters.name: value
parameters.doc: Value to encode; messagepack.null encodes as MessagePack nil.

fields.name: encode_empty_table_as_map
fields.doc: Encode empty tables as maps. Defaults to true; applies recursively.

elements.examples:
local bytes = messagepack.encode({name = "player", position = {1, 2, 3}})
local value = messagepack.decode(bytes)
assert(value.position[2] == 2)
local bytes = messagepack.encode({}, {encode_empty_table_as_map = false})
assert(bytes == string.char(0x90))

elements.name: messagepack.null
elements.brief:
Null light-userdata sentinel, identical to `json.null`. It encodes as
MessagePack nil. Decode with `decode_null_as_userdata = true` to retain
nil values in tables instead of dropping those Lua entries.
